text: For the one directing. According to Jeduthun. Of Asaph. A Psalm. 1 My voice [is] to God—indeed I cry out [with] my voice to God—and He has given ear to me.
In the day of my distress I sought the Lord; my hand in the night has been stretched out, and it does not slacken; my soul refuses to be comforted.
I remember God, and I groan; I meditate, and my spirit becomes faint. Selah
You hold the lids of my eyes; I am troubled, and I cannot speak.
I consider the days of old, the years of ages [past].
I remember, my song in the night; with my heart I converse, and my spirit searches.
“Will the Lord forever reject [us], and not anymore will He add to show favor?
Has His loving devotion ceased forever? Has [His] speech come to an end to generation and generation?
Or has God forgotten to show favor? Has He shut up in anger His compassion?” Selah
and I said, “I am grieved. Has it changed—the right hand of the Most High?”
I will remember the deeds of YAH; indeed, I will remember Your wonder of old.
And I have meditated on all Your work, and I put forth Your deeds.
O God, in holiness [is] Your way; what god [is] great like God?
You [are] the God doing wonders; You have made known among the peoples Your strength.
You have redeemed with [Your] arm a people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah
the waters saw You, O God, the waters saw You and swirled; even the depths trembled.
The clouds poured forth waters, the skies gave forth a voice, and Your arrows flashed back and forth.
The voice of Your thunder [was] in the whirlwind; the lightnings lit up the world; the earth trembled and shook.
Your way [was] in the sea, and Your paths in the great waters, and Your footprints were not known.
You led Your people like a flock, by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
